newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilt yields seen falling on RBI's rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilt yields seen falling on RBI's rate cut.

text.p: Yields on government securities will ease as a result of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s initiative on Wednesday to trigger a cut in interest rates, bankers said.
"Prices (of securities) will go up," Sanjay Bhasin, head of money markets at Standard Chartered Bank told Reuters.
"It should have an impact in lowering yields," he said.
The market will react especially on short-term maturities, dealers said.
"This is a signal for interest rates to come down," said Aashish Pitale, manager for debt research at ICICI Securities and Finance Company.
"I see secondary market yields reacting immediately... yields will fall," he said.
RBI said it was cutting the interest cap on deposits of 30 days to one year to 8.0 percent per annum from 9.0 percent.
By enabling banks to lower the cost of funds, RBI expects banks to lower their lending rates, analysts said.
The RBI announcement came at a time when the money market was unsettled by its decision to sell a medium-term bond on tap.

Gilt prices fell on Wednesday because of RBI's decision to sell the 12.59 percent 2004 stock at par (with accrued interest). The stock has been trading at a premium until RBI's decision triggered a crash in price, dealers said.
"RBI could have raised funds cheaper through another auction," said a money market dealer at a bank.
"Trading volumes fell and quotes became wider," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay.
"The trading will be nervous tomorrow," he added.
